items.title: Invoice Processing Bottlenecks Slowing Your Cash Flow Down
items.summary: Key Takeaways Poor invoice processing costs mid- to upper-midsized companies an estimated $2.3 million a month in lost efficiency. About 44% of companies say at least a quarter of their invoices run late every month. Most bottlenecks trace back to one thing: an invoice-to-cash loop that never closes without someone matching payments by hand. Manual data entry from paper and PDF invoices drives high error rates and slow posting. It’s also the easiest to fix, usually within weeks. The billing-to-cash disconnect is the hardest and highest-impact problem. Reconciling revenue in real time takes two to four months to get right. Slow approvals come from undefined approval paths, which push payments late and drive up days sales outstanding. Wiring invoice processing straight into automated cash application, instead of hiring more people, lets subscription revenue reconcile itself. Quick Summary Most invoice bottlenecks share one root: a billing cycle that won’t reconcile payments unless a person steps in. Invoices go out, payments trickle back, and your team burns hours matching the two. For SaaS companies on recurring and usage-based billing, that gap between billing and reconciled cash is exactly where momentum stalls.
